Everything here is Claude's proposal. n is every row not listed. Row names: lot, number, plenty, dozen, majority, dog, water, Kim, Toronto, numerous, rich, tall, and the category rows CN, PN, ADJ (any common noun, proper noun, or adjective may). ## The ten added features (from CGEL's lists)

### heads_nominal_after_separate_determiner
- definition: Reused from matrix-2026-10 (its definition in new_features.csv): in its primary use the form heads a nominal with a separate determiner before it (the few, the two, a dog, the rich). This is CGEL's first noun-typical dependent, 'certain determinatives' (ch. 5 §1 [2iii]). For the 139 forms, values are copied from new_feature_values.csv, NA read as n. (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [2iii])
- new rows: y: lot, number, dozen, majority, dog, water, rich, CN, ADJ; marginal: tall, PN
- basis, new rows: a lot, a number (CGEL p. 350: obligatory determiner); plenty takes none (p. 350); names in the primary use take none, except names that include the (the Hague); the rich; the tall only in contrasts (CGEL p. 417).
- existing forms: y: few, little, least, many, most, one_det, two_det, three_det; marginal: all, both, fewer, fewest, twice, several, some; blank: thrice, zero_det

### takes_prehead_AdjP_modifier
- definition: In its primary use, a restrictive pre-head AdjP modifies the nominal the form heads (good news, the lucky few, a huge lot of time). Non-restrictive adjectives (poor me, young Isaac Newton) are excluded; the exclamative lucky/poor/silly type has its own column (take_poor_lucky_silly_as_attrib_modifiers). (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [2iii]; ch. 6 §2 (adjectives aren't modified by adjectives))
- new rows: y: lot, number, dozen, majority, dog, water, CN; marginal: rich, ADJ
- basis, new rows: a whole/huge lot (CGEL p. 350); huge numbers (p. 350 [58]); plenty takes none (p. 350); the vast majority; the idle rich. Names n: in the primary use they take only non-restrictive adjectives (young Isaac Newton, CGEL pp. 520-521), a wider range than the pronouns' lucky/poor/silly, which the separate column records.
- existing forms: y: a_few, few, one_det, two_det, three_det; marginal: little, many
- basis, existing forms: the lucky few (corpus/premodification/2026-10-16-brett-supplied-adj-few.md); a lucky few; the remaining three; pronouns 'do not normally allow internal pre-head dependents' (CGEL p. 430).

### takes_relative_clause_modifier
- definition: An integrated relative clause modifies the nominal the form heads (people who work, those who came, we who have read the report). Delayed relatives (Who do you know who...) don't count. (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [2iii]; p. 430 for pronouns)
- new rows: y: lot, plenty, dozen, majority, dog, water, rich, CN, ADJ; marginal: number
- basis, new rows: there's a lot that I don't understand; the rich who live here; names take integrated relatives only in secondary uses.
- existing forms: y: a_few, a_great_many, a_little, all, any, anybody, anyone, anything, anywhere, everybody, everyone, everything, everywhere, few, little, least, many, more, most, much, none, nobody, no_one, nothing, nowhere, two_det, three_det, several, some, somebody, someone, something, somewhere, that, those, he, she, I, we_pron, you_pron_sing, you_pron_plur; marginal: another, both, each, enough, fewer, fewest, less, one_det, these, him, her_acc, me, one_pron, them_plur, they_plur, us_pron
- basis, existing forms: few who come ever leave, those who came, that which remains, something that you need to know (combined manuscript §2.4); I/We who have read the report, He who controls, you who worked (CGEL p. 430: personal pronouns with human denotation).

### takes_nonpartitive_complement
- definition: The form takes a complement other than a partitive of-phrase: an of-PP (a lot of people, a number of boys), another PP or clause (the fact that, proud of), or a than-phrase (more than ten). (Added by Claude, not on CGEL's lists: motivated by the quantity nouns' of-complements (CGEL pp. 349-350) and adjectives' complements (proud of))
- new rows: y: lot, number, plenty, dozen, majority, rich, CN, ADJ
- basis, new rows: a lot of people (CGEL p. 349 [54ii]); dozens of errors (p. 349 [53iii]); plenty of butter (p. 350); rich in minerals.
- existing forms: y: fewer, less, more; marginal: enough, sufficient
- basis, existing forms: than-phrases (more than ten); enough/sufficient with an infinitival (enough to go round).

### NP_functions_as_complement_in_PP
- definition: An NP headed by the form is the complement of a preposition (to the doctor, for some, to him). Dependent-only forms and nominative pronouns are n. (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [6i])
- new rows: y: lot, number, plenty, dozen, majority, dog, water, Kim, Toronto, rich, CN, PN, ADJ; marginal: tall
- basis, new rows: for the rich.
- existing forms: y: a_few, a_great_many, a_little, all, another, any, anybody, anyone, anything, anywhere, both, each, either, enough, everybody, everyone, everything, everywhere, few, fewer, little, less, least, many, more, most, much, neither, none, nobody, no_one, nothing, nowhere, one_det, two_det, three_det, once, several, some, somebody, someone, something, somewhere, that, these, this, those, which_int_det, whichever_int_det, each_other, one_another, him, himself, his, her_acc, hers, herself, it_plain, itself, me, mine, myself, one_pron, oneself, theirs_sing, theirs_plur, them_sing, them_plur, themself, themselves, us_pron, ours, ourselves, what_pron, whatever_pron, which_rel_pron, whom_int, whom_rel, whose_int, whoever, whomever, whosoever, you_pron_sing, you_pron_plur, yours_sing, yours_plur, yourself, yourselves, today, tomorrow, tonight, yesterday; marginal: fewest, sufficient, who_int, who_rel, whosever
- basis, existing forms: Dependent-only forms and nominative pronouns n; whose_int y (whose is that?).

### NP_functions_as_modifier_in_AdvP
- definition: An NP headed by the form modifies an AdvP (a whole day late, much later, that quickly, the sooner). (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [6v])
- new rows: y: lot, CN; marginal: plenty, ADJ
- basis, new rows: a lot later; a whole day late.
- existing forms: y: a_little, any, enough, less, more, much, no, somewhat, that, this, the; marginal: all, little, least, most
- basis, existing forms: much later, any sooner, no later, quickly enough, that quickly, the sooner.

### NP_functions_as_modifier_in_PP
- definition: An NP headed by the form modifies a PP (a mile under the sea, much before noon, all over the floor). (CGEL ch. 5 §1 [6vi])
- new rows: y: CN; marginal: lot
- basis, new rows: a mile under the sea.
- existing forms: y: a_little, all, much, somewhat; marginal: little
- basis, existing forms: much before noon; all over the floor; somewhat before.

### takes_post_head_AdjP
- definition: A post-head AdjP modifies the nominal the form heads (someone nice, the people present, those present, all present). (CGEL ch. 6 §2 [1i] (postpositive function))
- new rows: y: dog, water, CN; marginal: plenty, majority
- basis, new rows: a dog bigger than mine; water fit to drink.
- existing forms: y: all, anybody, anyone, anything, anywhere, everybody, everyone, everything, everywhere, little, much, nobody, no_one, nothing, nowhere, somebody, someone, something, somewhere, those; marginal: any, enough, few, many, none, several
- basis, existing forms: someone nice; all present; those present; Brett (19 Oct): all, much, and little take plain restrictors, few, some, and none take only comparatives (corpus/exclusion_tests/2026-10-19-brett-supplied-none-comparative.md).

### has_analytic_comparative
- definition: Graded by analytic more and most (more useful, more numerous). (CGEL ch. 6 §2 [1ii])
- new rows: y: numerous, ADJ; marginal: rich, tall
- existing forms: all n

### takes_ly_adverb_modifier
- definition: Modified by a degree or evaluative -ly adverb (remarkably happy, surprisingly few, considerably more); the approximators (almost, nearly, hardly, approximately) have their own columns and are excluded. (CGEL ch. 6 §2 [1iii]; p. 538 (the modifier test: nouns 'are modified by adjectives, not adverbs'))
- new rows: y: numerous, rich, tall, ADJ
- basis, new rows: remarkably numerous; nouns take adjectives, not adverbs.
- existing forms: y: few, fewer, little, less, many, more, much; marginal: least, most
- basis, existing forms: remarkably few, surprisingly many, relatively little, considerably more.
